title: A Pattern of Forgetting Begins
overview: After Joshua's death Israel turns to other gods, and the chapter sets out the repeating cycle of falling away, oppression, rescue and relapse that shapes the rest of the book.

parts.label: Weeping at Bokim (vv. 1-5)
parts.note: A messenger from the LORD says God kept his side of their agreement, but Israel made peace with the local peoples and left their altars standing, so those peoples will stay as a constant trouble and their gods as a snare. The people weep, giving the place its name, Bokim, meaning "weepers", though the rest of the chapter shows the sorrow did not lead to lasting change.

parts.label: Joshua dies (vv. 6-10)
parts.note: These verses repeat the ending of the book of Joshua, looking back to show how things went wrong. While people who had seen God's great acts were alive Israel stayed faithful, but the next generation grew up without knowing the LORD or that history.

parts.label: Turning to other gods (vv. 11-15)
parts.note: Israel worships Baal and Ashtoreth, a Canaanite god and goddess linked with storms, fertility and good harvests, and the plural forms here stand for all the local gods and goddesses. The text says plainly that the LORD in anger handed them over to raiders and fought against them, which the writer presents as the warned consequence of breaking faith.

parts.label: Judges rise and fall (vv. 16-19)
parts.note: The "judges" here are mainly leaders and rescuers whom God calls in a crisis, often over just one region, not courtroom officials. Each brings relief while alive, but after each one dies the people slide back even further, a cycle the rest of the book acts out story by story.

parts.label: Nations left as a test (vv. 20-23)
parts.note: Because Israel broke its agreement, God says he will no longer drive out the peoples still in the land but will use them to test whether Israel stays loyal. Verse 23 adds that this is also why Joshua had not conquered everyone.

think: What do you think gets lost when a generation grows up without remembering what shaped the one before it?
